artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Opium is the second studio album by British multi-instrumentalist Matt Berry, originally released in 2005. The album blends elements of rock, folk, and country, with a distinct 1970s-inspired sound that features lush arrangements, melodic guitar work, and Berry’s rich, theatrical vocals. Its warm, organic production and introspective songwriting evoke a sense of nostalgia, drawing comparisons to classic British pop and psychedelic folk acts. The record stands out for its seamless fusion of genres and Berry’s signature blend of melancholy and whimsy.

Within Matt Berry’s discography, Opium marks a pivotal early work that helped establish his reputation as a distinctive voice in the UK’s alternative music scene. It preceded his later, more widely recognized albums and set the template for his evolving style—characterized by vintage instrumentation and a cinematic sensibility. Though Opium did not chart upon its original release, it gained a cult following and critical acclaim for its craftsmanship and originality. The album was later reissued by Acid Jazz Records, further cementing its status as a foundational release in Berry’s career.
